why: Rule 1+3 point here within the cluster (the 139 cm muon cools toward 14006 and Braggs at 14002 where an 18 cm Michel trail hangs off), but 14006 is a bare track end 4.7 cm from the y=200 face with no hadronic activity, so the pick is close to a guess.
Rule 1: degree-4 apex with a 90 cm proton rising to 195600 at 16005, a 7 cm 149-165k proton stub, a 292 cm muon and a 62 cm pion, all leaving; zoom shows a clean 4-prong junction.

Rule 1: 2 of 2 prongs rise away - the 30 cm proton follows the template monotonically up to 193660 at 14000 and the 15 cm muon rises to 14001, with a 106 degree opening so it is not a single scattered track.
Rule 1 on a nearly empty event: the only fitted object is an 8 cm proton that rises from 146498 at 13002 to 202836 at 13000, so it stops at 13000 and starts at 13002 amid the nearby sub-cm dots.
Rule 1: the contained 227 cm muon is flat MIP at 12001 and spikes to 235000 at 12000 (stopping end), and the only other deposits (5 cm 'e' cluster 22 and cluster 52) sit right on top of 12001.

The 257 cm track leaves the detector at z=499.9 (13000), so the contained upstream end 13002 is the start; it also carries a 365000 e/cm point and the small clusters 39009/40011 sit within 10 cm of it.
Rule 1+3: the 174 cm muon rises monotonically along the template to 180000 at 10000 where a sub-cm Michel-like blob (36007) sits, so the cool 58002 end 10002 is the start.

Rule 1: 2 of 2 rise away - a 255000 e/cm proton stub to 17001 and a 47 cm muon to 17000 - inside the busiest region (3-prong EM blob 77034 plus 55008/57012 within 7 cm); tier dropped because the two prongs are 166 degrees apart.
Rule 1+3: a 4 cm 117256 e/cm proton stub sits at 14004 and the 97.7 cm muon rises away to 113810 at 14003, where a 15.6 cm 'e' Michel plus blobs 45019/39007 mark the stopping end; 97 degree opening.

Rule 1: the 76 cm heavily-ionising track follows the proton template monotonically down from 235000 at 7000, so it stops there; 7001 is the start, with only a single-point spike (not a Bragg) and blob 24008 beside it.
Rule 8 territory - just two isolated blobs; I take the cooler, lower-z end of the only fitted 18 cm segment, but the three sub-cm dots at z=200-210 are an equally arbitrary choice.
Rule 1: degree-5 apex at the lowest z in the cluster with a 65 cm proton rising to 189221, a 115 cm muon leaving toward the z=500 wall and a 33 cm pion, 3 of 5 prongs rising away.

Rule 1: two proton prongs both rise away - the 13 cm one climbs the proton template monotonically to 208127 at 68030 and the 30 cm one to 127893 - at 106 degrees, with the MIP muon chain (70/71/65/66 into cluster 22) leaving in -x.

Rule 1: degree-3 apex with a 61 cm proton rising to 185480 at 13000, a 5 cm 145000 e/cm proton stub, and an 89 cm muon rising to 113577 at 13001; the two long prongs are 154 degrees apart but the zoom confirms the hot 13004 stub is a genuine third prong.
Rule 1 on a single-prong event: the 28 cm proton rises from 120115 at 4003 to 180023 at 4000, so it stops at 4000 and started at the lower-z end 4003.
